No tests or other evidence of checking are visible.

terms.meaning: Splitting a long list into numbered pages so only one page of rows shows at a time.
A panel that slides in from the edge of the screen to hold a form, here the filters.
A set of tick boxes where a visitor can choose several options from one list.
Values a component remembers while the page is open, such as the current page number.

used_by: Not visible in the code shown. The Home page links here with stage, maturity and segment values.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and building blocks
sections.what: Brings in the parts the page uses: data fetching, the table and card layouts, filter controls, the map, the timeline slider, link helpers, and the citation tools that open source details.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: evField, SortKey
sections.title: Evidence wrapper and sort keys
sections.what: Packages a table cell's value with its evidence, such as the source link, publisher, exact quote and location in the source. When no evidence exists, the fields are left empty rather than filled in. It also lists the columns that can be sorted.
sections.why: The code comment says missing evidence must stay honest, showing nothing rather than invented values.
sections.watch_out: Only the first evidence item for each field is used, so a value with several sources shows only one of them.

sections.name: COLUMNS, STATUS_OPTIONS, STAGE_OPTIONS, MATURITY_OPTIONS, PIPELINE_STAGES
sections.title: Column layout and filter option lists
sections.what: Defines the table's columns with their titles and widths, and which ones can be sorted. Operator and COD cannot be sorted. It also holds the fixed lists of status, stage and maturity options, and the set of stages that count as pipeline (not yet operating).
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The fixed lists suggest the options are known in advance.
sections.watch_out: The status, stage and maturity lists are typed in by hand. A new value added to the data will not appear as a filter option until this file is updated.

sections.name: getUniqueValues
sections.title: Unique value helper
sections.what: Returns the distinct, non-empty values for one field across all rows, sorted alphabetically. It feeds the country and technology filter choices.
sections.why: Likely reason: builds the filter choices from the data so they always match what exists.
sections.watch_out: Empty and zero values are dropped. A genuine zero in such a field would not appear as a choice.

sections.name: formatNa
sections.title: Blank value label
sections.what: Shows a grey not-available label when a value is missing, and otherwise returns the value unchanged.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page must show a clear blank rather than a misleading zero or an empty cell.
sections.watch_out: Only null, undefined and empty text count as missing. Zero is shown as zero, which is intended.

sections.name: formatBudget
sections.title: Budget formatting
sections.what: Formats a single budget value for display, using the shared display rules for the industry and currency. Missing budgets show the not-available label.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Delegating to a shared function keeps budget display the same across pages.
sections.watch_out: The result depends on the industry and currency being passed in correctly, so a missing currency can show the wrong unit.

sections.name: formatBudgetCell
sections.title: Budget cell choice
sections.what: Chooses the best budget to show in a cell. It prefers a low-to-high range, then the planned budget, then the older budget field, then the raw budget text with a document icon. If none exist, it shows not-available.
sections.why: Likely reason: projects store budgets in different forms, and the page should show the most specific one available.
sections.watch_out: Raw budget text is displayed as typed and cannot be sorted or compared, unlike the numeric budgets.

sections.name: capacityValueUnit
sections.title: Capacity value and unit
sections.what: Works out the capacity number and its unit for a project. Nuclear projects use the older megawatt field. Other industries use the general capacity value and its unit. Missing capacity stays empty rather than becoming zero.
sections.why: The code comment says nuclear keeps its original display and other industries store capacity with their own units, so the unit must not be mislabeled.
sections.watch_out: A non-nuclear project with no capacity value can still carry a unit, which may show a unit with no number.

sections.name: renderCapacityCell
sections.title: Capacity cell text
sections.what: Builds the capacity text for a table cell. The column header already says MW, so the unit is shown only when it is different, such as kilotonnes per year.
sections.why: The code comment says the header already shows MW, so repeating it in each cell would clutter the table.
sections.watch_out: If the column header text changes, the unit may disappear from the cells even though the data still has it.

sections.name: capacityInline
sections.title: Capacity text for map panel
sections.what: Builds the capacity text for the map side panel, which has no column header, so the unit is always shown. A missing value shows a plain dash.
sections.why: The code comment says the map panel has no header, so the unit must be shown inline.
sections.watch_out: The map panel uses a dash for missing values while the table uses the not-available label, so the same missing value looks different in each view.

sections.name: statusVariant
sections.title: Status colour rule
sections.what: Maps each project status to a badge style. Completed is outlined, on track is the default, critical risk and over budget are red, and delayed and paused are secondary. Any other status uses the default style.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The colours appear to highlight risk at a glance.
sections.watch_out: An unknown status falls back to the default style, so a new status can look healthy by accident.

sections.name: computeDateBounds
sections.title: Earliest and latest milestone dates
sections.what: Scans the rows for a chosen milestone date and finds the earliest and latest date. Those values set the ends of the timeline slider. If no dates exist, it returns nothing and the slider is replaced by a message.
sections.why: Likely reason: the slider should only cover dates that actually appear in the data.
sections.watch_out: Dates are compared as plain text, so they only sort correctly if they use a consistent year-first format.

sections.name: CheckboxGroup
sections.title: Reusable checkbox group
sections.what: Draws a labeled list of checkboxes. Clicking one adds or removes that option from the selected list and passes the new list back to the parent. Underscores in option names are shown as spaces.
sections.why: Likely reason: the same checkbox pattern is needed for status, stage, maturity, country and technology filters.
sections.watch_out: The test ids are built from the option names in lowercase, so renaming an option also changes its test id.

sections.name: Explore (part 1)
sections.title: Page state and data requests
sections.what: Starts the Explore page. It reads the current industry and defaults to nuclear when none is set. It keeps the toggles and paging state, then builds two requests: one for the current page of projects and one for up to 500 rows used for the timeline and filter choices.
sections.why: The code shows the page is scoped to one industry and sends filters, sorting and paging to the server so the browser handles one page at a time.
sections.watch_out: Without an industry, the page quietly shows nuclear data. The timeline and filter choices come from only 500 rows, so larger datasets may hide some dates and options.

sections.name: Explore (part 2)
sections.title: Results, filter options and citation tools
sections.what: Reads the project rows and total from the server response, works out how many pages exist, and builds the timeline range. It sets up the citation drawer and the map marker source panel, and keeps local copies of the filter values for the filter panel.
sections.why: Likely reason: the local copies let users edit filters without changing the results until they press Apply.
sections.watch_out: The local copies reset whenever the saved filters change, so any unsaved edits in the filter panel are lost.

sections.name: Explore (part 3)
sections.title: Apply, clear and timeline handlers
sections.what: Apply saves the chosen filters, returns to page one, and closes the panel. Clear empties both the local and saved filters. Moving the timeline sets a date range and turns the slider on. Changing the milestone type turns the slider off and clears the range.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Resetting to page one after a filter change avoids showing an empty later page.
sections.watch_out: Changing the milestone type silently clears any date range the user set on the slider.

sections.name: Explore (part 4)
sections.title: Project list and sorting
sections.what: Turns each server row into the shape the table and map need, adding fields such as country, units, budgets and evidence. Clicking a column header asks the server to sort by it, flipping direction if the same column is clicked again. Clicking a row opens that project's page.
sections.why: The code sends sort settings to the server, so the full list is sorted before paging.
sections.watch_out: Sorting happens on the server, but only the current page of 50 rows is shown, so the order makes sense only across pages the server returns.

sections.name: Explore (part 5)
sections.title: Result count, timeline and milestone controls
sections.what: Shows the current result count, page number, the milestone selector and the timeline slider with a clear button. The header counts show loading dots while the data is fetched.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The count label shows the number of rows on this page next to the overall total, which can be read as the number on screen rather than the number matching the filters.

sections.name: Explore (part 6)
sections.title: Table view: headers and first cells
sections.what: Draws the table view. Each column header can be clicked to sort. Each row shows the project name with a PRIS badge when an IAEA reference exists, then the country, technology, units and capacity cells. Each value can open its citation.
sections.why: Likely reason: the owner can see each value and check its source directly from the table.
sections.watch_out: The table has a minimum width of 1200 pixels, so on narrow screens it must be scrolled sideways.

sections.name: Explore (part 7)
sections.title: Table view: remaining cells
sections.what: Fills the rest of each table row: stage, status, maturity, likelihood, confidence, budgets, delay, EPC, vendor, operator and COD. When a revised COD date exists, the original date is struck through and the revised date is highlighted.
sections.why: Likely reason: showing the revised COD with the original beside it makes schedule changes visible at a glance.
sections.watch_out: The stage and status cells call text methods directly on the value with no check, so a project with no stage or status could crash the table. Likelihood shows Not assessed when it is empty.

sections.name: Explore (part 8)
sections.title: Map view side panel
sections.what: Shows the map and a side panel titled Projects in viewport. The panel lists the first five projects with name, country, capacity and status, and notes how many more exist. Clicking an entry opens that project.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives a list beside the map for quick access without leaving the map view.
sections.watch_out: The panel title says viewport, but it lists the first five projects of the loaded page, not the projects visible on the map.

sections.name: Explore (part 9)
sections.title: Page number controls
sections.what: Shows First, Prev, numbered page buttons, Next and Last, but only when there is more than one page. The numbered buttons show at most seven pages around the current one.
sections.why: Likely reason: so a visitor can move between pages of projects quickly.
sections.watch_out: The window of page numbers uses different formulas near the start, middle and end, so changing the page count logic needs a check at each edge.

sections.name: Explore (part 10)
sections.title: Filter drawer top section
sections.what: Closes the filter drawer and draws its Apply and Clear All buttons, a search box that applies on Enter, and checkbox groups for status, lifecycle stage and maturity.
sections.why: Likely reason: the filters are held in local copies so nothing changes until Apply is pressed.
sections.watch_out: Filter choices are only copied into the real filter state when Apply is pressed, so a missed click leaves the list unchanged.

sections.name: Explore (part 11)
sections.title: Filter drawer remaining fields
sections.what: Adds checkbox groups for country and technology, and a minimum and maximum megawatt box, then closes the drawer and places the citation drawer.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code for the choice of fields. The megawatt range is a numeric filter, so these boxes let a visitor narrow by size.
sections.watch_out: The megawatt boxes hold text, so whatever reads them must convert to numbers, and an empty box must mean no limit. That handling is not visible here.

summary: Project list page with page-number controls and a side drawer of database filters, as far as the visible code shows.
purpose: Lets a visitor browse many projects one page at a time and narrow them with filters such as status, stage, maturity, country, technology and megawatt range.
why: Likely reason: a long project list is hard to use all at once, so it is split into pages and filters are kept in a drawer to save screen space.
how: 1. Builds a list of value options for the filter checkboxes. 2. Shows the filter drawer with a search box, checkbox groups and a megawatt range. 3. Applies filters only when the Apply button or Enter is pressed. 4. Shows page controls only when there is more than one page. Most of the file, including the data loading and table, was not visible, so the full flow is unknown.
inputs: The visitor's clicks on page buttons, filter checkboxes, the search box and the megawatt inputs. Filter values may also come from the web address, as the Home page links use the stage, maturity and segment names.
outputs: A filtered, paged list of projects and a filter drawer. The visible code does not show what is sent to the server.
risks: Filter values typed into the megawatt boxes are text, so any code that compares them must convert them to numbers. That conversion is not visible here. Local filter choices are lost if the Apply button is not pressed.
debug: If the page count looks wrong, check the page state and total pages values. If a filter does nothing, check that Apply was pressed and that the filter value reaches the data request. The data loading code was not visible, so read the top of the file.
